- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias in second half of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp rise followed by decline, model often misses the dip; reduce forecast in 2nd half by 1–3%.
- Sentiment + price momentum: if sentiment >0.6 and price >70, forecast should be capped at 75–80 to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment is flat (0.2–0.4) and price is trending, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5 point bias toward trend direction.
